newsitem.title: USA: Snyder Oil has exploratory success.
newsitem.headline: Snyder Oil has exploratory success.

text.p: Snyder Oil Corp said Thursday that the A-2 exploratory well at its High Island Block 208 prospect offshore Texas logged pay in two separate sand intervals which were tested at a combined rate of 18.6 million cubic feet of gas per day and 160 barrels of condensate per day.
SOCO Offshore Inc, a subsidiary of Snyder Oil, is operator of High Island Block 208 and holds a 60 percent working interest in the well.
Phillips Petroleum owns the remaining 40 percent.
The A-2 well should begin production from the High Island 208 "A" platform by June, Snyder said.
The company also said it has had continued development success at its offshore Main Pass complex.
Snyder said that during the quarter the A-12 well of the Main Pass Block 259 ("Pabst Field") was drilled to a measured depth of 15,323 feet and completed in the Tex W-6 sand.

The well is currently producing at a rate of about 13 million cubic feet of gas and 2,600 barrels of condensate per day through a 41/64 inch choke with 4,150 pounds per square inch flowing tubing pressure, the company said.
Snyder said the A-11ST well of the Main Pass Block 259 has been completed and the flowline is being installed and the well is expected to be on production within a week.
Based on log results, the well encountered about 40 feet of pay in the 7700 foot sand interval.
Also during the first quarter, the A-2 well was recompleted in the 10,300 foot sand interval.
The well is flowing at an approximate daily rate of 12 million cubic feet of gas and 200 barrels of condensate.
Snyder also said it has a preliminary natural gas gathering agreement which will expand its deliverability at the field significantly by early 1998.

It said that SOCO Offshore has entered into an agreement with Viosca Knoll Gathering Co to expand its existing gathering system in the Main Pass area, which would enable the company to increase production from the Pabst and Busch platforms to about 175 million cubic feet of gas per day.
Such expansion is expected to be in service by early 1998.

Snyder said that the combined production capacity from the Pabst and Busch platforms is currently in excess of 150 million cubic feet of gas per day, but production levels have from time to time been limited to 100 million cubic feet of gas per day due to existing pipeline constraints.
The company expects substantial further production increases in the Main Pass area from beginning production from its Main Pass 261 ("Ingrid") Field.
